answer: An agent market requires each active identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before bidding on work. Creating a thousand fake agents therefore ties up a thousand bonds; recycling identities cannot free the capital sooner. Each identity is an island of locked funds, so even at the zenith of a sybil campaign, scale carries a proportional cost. Through this prism, cheap names become expensive bidding power, costing the attacker liquidity and forgone returns.
